evidence.requirements: Almost every functional requirement is met. The three tastings are hard-coded with the brief's data (server/app.js:6-10). The start page shows title, date/time, price and '<n> seats left' (App.jsx:52-57, start.jpg). There are 'Book <title>' links (App.jsx:58). The form has Name/Email/Guests fields and a 'Book' button (App.jsx:115-118). Guests are limited to 1-8 and seat limits are enforced on the server (app.js:48-56). Errors appear under their field (form.jpg). The confirmation shows the 'Booking confirmed' heading, tasting, guests, total and reference (confirmation.jpg). /staff has a Password field and Sign in button and reads STAFF_PASSWORD (app.js:20, App.jsx:146-147). Bookings are grouped by tasting with Cancel, and cancelling frees seats (app.js:83-94, staff.jpg). There is a fully-booked state (App.jsx:55-56, 108-109). Partly met: the Process requirement. The repo has no spec, plan, ADR or review artefacts, so there is no evidence of the specify/plan/review phases. Usable on a phone is only implied by the responsive grid and media query (styles.css:24,72); no mobile screenshot shows it. No form library was used, but the brief only gave one as an example, so that is acceptable.
evidence.correctness: The seat check and the push run synchronously in one handler (app.js:52-58). Node is single-threaded, so concurrent requests cannot overbook. Cancelling removes the booking, so seatsLeft is recomputed (app.js:26,92). Guests are validated as an integer from 1 to 8, and numeric strings are accepted (app.js:48-49). The 409 response gives a specific message such as 'Only N seats left' or 'fully booked' (app.js:54). The client reloads seats after an error (App.jsx:83). Malformed JSON returns a JSON 400 (app.js:103-104, test). Minor issues: old field errors are not cleared while the user edits. Booking references are not checked for collisions; the risk is negligible. Staff sessions never expire. Cancel acts immediately with no confirmation step (App.jsx:165).
evidence.security: React escapes all output and there is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. The password check hashes both values with SHA-256 and compares them with timingSafeEqual (app.js:14-17). An empty or unset STAFF_PASSWORD disables login (app.js:69, tested). The session token comes from randomUUID and is set in an HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict cookie (app.js:71-73). Logout invalidates the session on the server (app.js:77-80). Staff API routes are guarded (app.js:83,89). There are no secrets in the code. Gaps: no Secure cookie flag, no session expiry, the in-memory session set is unbounded, there is no rate limit against brute-forcing the password, and there are no security headers.
evidence.code_quality: The structure is small and clear: createApp is a factory so it can be tested (app.js:20), index.js is thin, and the UI is one App.jsx with small components (Field, Status, useLoad). Naming is good and errors are handled consistently ({errors:{field}} for field-level errors, a generic JSON error handler). Some code is very dense, which hurts readability: chained ternaries (app.js:48), one-line promise chains (App.jsx:135,139), and a useLoad hook that disables exhaustive-deps (App.jsx:19).
evidence.tests: api.test.js covers the listing, booking total and reference, seat reduction, a table of invalid inputs, numeric strings, the seat limit and fully booked responses, the 404, the staff 401, the wrong password, the disabled login, grouped listing with cancel freeing seats, logout and malformed JSON. ui.test.jsx drives the real server end to end with RTL. It covers the guest flow including a field error linked through aria-describedby, the sold-out display, and staff sign-in, listing and cancel. Weaknesses: the UI tests share server state and depend on test order (the staff test relies on Anna's booking from the guest test). There is no UI test for the over-limit 409 message next to the field, even though the second test's name says it covers that. There is no concurrency test.
evidence.ux_design: The screenshots show a coherent winery look: a burgundy header with a gold rule, serif headings, cream background, and cards with a green seats badge (start.jpg). The inline error is clear, with a red border and message (form.jpg). The confirmation is clean and green with a definition list (confirmation.jpg). The staff tables are tidy (staff.jpg). Weaknesses: dates are shown raw as '2026-11-06 18:00' with no weekday or friendly format. There is no imagery or extra detail about each tasting. Cancel has no confirmation step.
evidence.accessibility: Labels are tied to inputs with htmlFor/id. Fields set aria-invalid and aria-describedby to the error text (App.jsx:28-34). lang='en' is set, and the page uses header, main, footer, h1/h2 and a dl. Focus-visible gets a gold outline (styles.css:14). Form-level alerts use role=alert. Gaps: field-level errors are not announced (no live region) and focus does not move to the first invalid field. The confirmation relies on aria-live on a section that is newly mounted, which is often not announced, and focus is not moved to it. The action column header is empty (App.jsx:161). <time> elements have no dateTime attribute. Text contrast looks adequate.
evidence.simplicity: There are 4 runtime dependencies (express, react, react-dom, react-router-dom) and about 300 lines of app code. That fits the problem exactly, with no needless layers.
evidence.maintainability: There is no README, so STAFF_PASSWORD, the run, build and test steps and the dev proxy are not documented anywhere except the console warning in index.js:4. There are no docs, specs, ADRs or staff manual. There is no CI configuration. Versions use carets, although a package-lock.json is present. engines is 'node >=22' and there is no .nvmrc. There is no versioning or release approach beyond version 1.0.0. The test suite is a solid regression base, and the in-memory shortcut is noted in a comment (app.js:19).
evidence.visual_design: Typography is consistent: Georgia headings with system sans body text. The burgundy, gold and cream palette is used the same way on every page, and green marks success. Spacing and rounded cards are even across start.jpg, form.jpg, confirmation.jpg and staff.jpg. It looks finished, though fairly plain, with no imagery or logo.
evidence.layout: Hierarchy is clear. Start page: hero, then a three-column card grid with the CTA at the bottom of each card. Form and confirmation pages: a centred panel. Staff page: a heading with Sign out, then one panel per tasting holding a table that scrolls horizontally on small screens (styles.css:67). No overlap or clipping is visible. On desktop a lot of space is left empty below the cards (start.jpg).
evidence.usability: Guests book in one click and a short form. There is a back link, the guests field is pre-filled with 2, errors sit next to their fields, and the confirmation has a back button. Fully booked tastings hide the Book button. Staff can find the footer link, and sign-in and cancel are straightforward. Minor issues: Cancel has no confirmation or undo, errors persist while the user edits, and dates are shown in ISO format.
evidence.reception: Guests would see it as a trustworthy, professional winery booking page (start.jpg, confirmation.jpg), and staff get a clear overview (staff.jpg). It would be better received with a friendlier date format and a bit more content about each tasting.

unmet_requirements: Process: no spec, plan, ADR or review artefacts in the repository, so there is no evidence that the configured specify/plan/test-first/review process was followed
Usable on a phone: plausible from the responsive CSS but no mobile screenshot shows it (partly verified)
strengths: Booking logic is correct and safe: seats are checked and reserved synchronously on the server, validation is thorough and errors come back per field, and cancelling frees seats

Staff auth is sound: timing-safe password comparison, a random-token HttpOnly SameSite=Strict cookie, logout that invalidates the session on the server, and login disabled when STAFF_PASSWORD is unset
Lean, coherent implementation (Express + React Router, 4 runtime dependencies) with a polished, consistent winery look and meaningful API and end-to-end UI tests
issues: No README, docs, CI or ADRs: STAFF_PASSWORD, the run, build and test steps and the dev workflow are undocumented, and there is no evidence of the required process artefacts
Accessibility gaps: field errors are not announced and focus is not moved to the first invalid field or to the confirmation; the action column header is empty
Staff Cancel deletes immediately with no confirmation, sessions never expire and logins are not rate-limited; guests see raw ISO dates instead of friendly ones
review.verdict: This is a correct, compact and visually polished booking app that meets the brief's functional requirements, with sound seat handling, solid staff auth and good tests. It needs a README and CI, better announcement of errors and success for screen readers, and a confirmation step for Cancel before it is fully ready for the winery.
